chapter_theme: The close of Subramaniar Njanam: the pranayama in full, with VINN fixed in the suzhumunai, VANG filling at the root, SING letting out and ANG retaining at the throat; the vaasi rises to the lotus whorl and comes to live in the body; Shakti's meditation with ANG SING and ash, during which Parashakti dances; Agastya is told to drink the moon-nectar at the whorl, shown the summit of the adharas, the six-faced state at the end of sound and the vel's point that is silence, and sent to Sathuragiri and Pothigai to practise the eightfold yoga at the guru's feet. Murugan climbs the summit of the cosmic bound and delights in the vel of Om, as in the invocation.
structure_note: 2511 and 2512 give the breath with its four syllables and the vaasi's rise; 2513 and 2514 Shakti's meditation and the nectar; 2515 the stations shown to Agastya; 2516 his dispatch to the southern hills; 2517 Murugan's ascent and the colophon முற்றே.

2511.reading: Doing pranayama with awareness, hear the working, Siva Siva; the prana-air will not go false, hear the novelty of its standing joined and at play: gently fix 'VINN' in the suzhumunai; as the seat, fill at the root with 'VANG'; truly let out in the suzhumunai with 'SING'; and swiftly retain at the throat with 'ANG'.
2511.nuance: The fullest statement of the work's breath formula: four syllables for four acts and places, with கும்பே (retain) at the throat (கண்டம்) added to 2501's fill and let out. கருமானம் is read as 'working' or 'operation'; the word is uncertain. சுழுனை is a shortened spelling of சுழுமுனை.

2512.reading: Retaining at the throat with 'ANG', the vaasi, the holy vaasi, unmoving, climbs to the body of the red-lotus whorl, turns, goes into that body and lives there; with care, itself as itself within itself, standing in its own nature the vaasi plays; auspiciously fixing 'VINN' in the suzhumunai, with method remain as this world and the beyond, and see.
2512.nuance: பிண்டம் (the body) is where the breath comes to dwell after rising to the whorl (சுழி), which tradition places at the crown; the verse's picture is of the breath returning to live in the body rather than leaving it. இகபரம் (this world and the beyond) is what the practitioner becomes, not where he goes.

2513.reading: To see, hear the meditation of Shakti, told as the seed; recite ANG SING, make sixteen repetitions with intelligence, smear the fine ash powder visibly, and purely Parashakti will dance; meditating in this way, see truly the firmness of pranayama.
2513.nuance: The dance of Parashakti is what the meditation produces, and it is tested by the steadiness of the breath. ANG and SING are the retaining and releasing syllables of 2511, so Shakti's meditation is the breath's two halves; the sixteen repetitions match 2502.

2514.reading: Firm great sage Agastya, listen: meditating on true Shakti, like the blaze of sun and moon, knowing the seat of the five agents, doing pranayama steadily, abiding at Pothigai which is the meaning of the sruti, mounting the vaasi of the kala of life's pleasant breath, with the mind made one standing at the whorl, take the untroubled drink of nectar.
2514.nuance: அமிர்தபானம் is the yogic nectar held to flow at the crown when the breath is raised, as the next verse's மதியமிர்தம் (moon-nectar) confirms; it is tradition's reading and the verse's own image. பஞ்ச கர்த்தாள் are the five agents of the five acts. Pothigai, Agastya's hill, is called the meaning of the Veda.

2515.reading: Taking the moon-nectar called the drink, he showed the way of the whorl that is Parabrahman, told the method of pranayama that knows the adhara called the seat and the adhara above it, showed the state called jnana and the root, showed the six-faced station at the end of sound, and showed the point of the vel that is silence; knowing that point, stopping the kala, stand on the crown.
2515.nuance: The list is a map of the body's stations as Murugan shows them, and it ends by making Murugan himself a station: ஆறுமுக நிலையம் at நாதாந்தம், the end of sound, and the vel's point as மோனம், silence. The god of the legend becomes the state the breath reaches.

2516.reading: Go to the summit of Sathuragiri and dwell at steady Pothigai; becoming yourself, fixing 'VINN', when you recite with meditation the one mantra you have thought in your mind, it will be attained purely; standing still, go by the eightfold yoga and stand clearly at the feet of the guru Sivaya.
2516.nuance: Sathuragiri and Pothigai are the Siddhars' southern hills, and this is the work's version of Agastya's sending to the south. சும்மா நின்று (standing still, doing nothing) is a Siddhar phrase for the effortless state, set here beside the labour of the eight limbs.

2517.reading: Seeing himself by the clarity of clarities, giving Agastya the imperishable boon of grace that he remain firm and do tapas forever, the peacock-hero with the vel eagerly went to the summit of the imperishable cosmic bound, became king of the eight-hill mountain, and, ceasing, being himself everywhere in the cosmic void, delighted in the vel shaped as Om: the end.
2517.nuance: அட்டகிரி பாவதம் (the eight-hill mountain) is unexplained; it may be the mountains of the eight directions or Murugan's hill shrines. ஒழிவாகி can be 'ceasing' or 'becoming the remainder'. The verse repeats the invocation's அண்டவரை முடி and ஓங்கார வடிவேல், so the work ends where it began.

links.note: Tirumular measures the breath: sixteen in by the left, thirty-two out by pingala, sixty-four held between. Subramaniar gives the same three acts, with a fourth place, as syllables at body-stations: VANG at the root, SING in the suzhumunai, ANG at the throat. Counts in one, letters in the other.

Sivavakkiyar's vaasi rises gently on the silent five letters into the filled light, where he and I mingle and no one remains; here the vaasi climbs to the whorl, returns to live in the body, and the practitioner becomes this world and the beyond. Both end the breath's rise in a state past the self.

Tirumular's yogis bind the breath and taste the nectar of knowledge-bliss from the bright moon; Agastya is told to raise the vaasi, stand at the whorl and take the untroubled nectar, which the next verse calls moon-nectar.
The invocation names the vel the shape of Om; here the vel's point is silence and the six-faced station is at the end of sound. The work moves from Om as the vel to what lies past sound at its tip.

Tirumular lists the eight limbs, from yama to samadhi; Agastya is sent to go by the eightfold yoga (அட்டாங்க யோகம்) to the guru's feet. The verse names the discipline and relies on Tirumular's kind of enumeration for its content.

In Tirumular Siva sends Agastya south to stand first in the tilting world; here Murugan sends him to Sathuragiri and Pothigai. The two texts share Agastya's commission to the south, but the sender differs.
The summit of the cosmic bound (அண்டவரை முடி) and the vel shaped as Om (ஓங்கார வடிவேல்) open and close the work; the invocation states the practice and the colophon shows Murugan performing it.
